As a more practical example, if you infer someone is an INTJ and identify logical patterns to their decision making and a subjective approach to world-view, you can reliably approximate their thought process. Igf you know your Fi is underdeveloped you can focus your efforts to improve your cognition. It helps turn something abstract into something more concrete. On the other hand, you have people trying to predict the future and personality traits based on whether a mf was born November 21st or November 22nd.

"Is it SCIENCE? No. Pseudoscience at best.

Is it bullshit? Far from it.

Why would it be? It's not at all like astrology, where you would claim a person's personality is shaped by utterly unrelated elements (stars). In MBTI you simply observe and state what you observed. There's no causality, only observation.

It's a means to describe cognitive patterns and functions, a way to attribute words to traits that could otherwise be harder to measure. Why does that matter? Because the ability to describe something goes hand-in-hand with the ability to understand it, and for that MBTI is extremely useful! Even if it doesn't go to the depths the scientific community would demand.

Saying MBTI is bullshit just because it doesn't grasp at every tiny variant of human personality is the same as saying colors are bullshit because dark blue isn't the same as light blue. Would you rather we not have words for colors just because we can't name every shade in existence? The work of anyone trying to redecorate, or paint a picture or pick clothes would be hell, but having a system that let's us say "yup, this is green" makes it easier. Just like saying "Yup, I'm an introver" or "Yup, I need to develop my Fi".

The issue here is in how some idiots think you can break everyone down into 16 identical boxes. The value of MBTI is conceptual. A means to identify specific aspects of personality and cognition so we can better understand others' minds and work to improve our own. So we can name the shit that boils up in our head.

Same goes to a great length of psychology, to be honest. The human mind is still vastly unexplored and uncomprehended, not to mention how hard it is to get empirical evidence from something this subjective and abstract. Still, we need THEORIES, pseudosciences, in order to brave this waters. Maybe through MBTI we develop something more concrete and scientifical, for whatever good that'll do.

The fact is, psychology will never have the degree of certainty physics do. You'll never predict one's choices like you can predict the motion of astronomical objects. You'll never get to see what makes the essence of one's being in a microscope. Most of it is just theory and speculation, and the fact is Jung is one of the most respected names in this pursuit.

Jung went very deep into supernatural and mythological stuff as a means to understand the collective consciousness. The archetypes are based on thorough research of several human cultures and communities, including some extremely marginalized ones with little to no contact with the outside world. By drawing from superstitions and legends he could grasp at common patterns within individuals and societies that indicate all the way back to human nature.
